title: Willing to Go All the Way In

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses entered the cloud as he went on up the mountain. And he stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights." - Exodus 24:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends with a simple but remarkable sentence. Moses enters the cloud — the very cloud that looked like consuming fire to everyone watching below — and stays there forty days and forty nights. While the people saw fire and kept their distance, Moses walked in. And he did not visit briefly; he remained.

What courage and what love for God this shows. Moses had learned that the God who appears fearsome from a distance is the God who welcomes those He calls. He did not let fear keep him at the edge. He went all the way in, and he stayed long enough for God to speak, to teach, to give. Deep encounters with God are rarely rushed.

There is an invitation here for us. Many of us stay at a safe distance in our walk with God — near enough to observe, not close enough to be changed. We give Him hurried moments rather than sustained attention. But God calls us to enter in and remain. Jesus said it plainly: abide in me (John 15:4). Not a quick visit, but a settled dwelling. Do not be content to watch the fire from below. Step in, stay a while, and let God do His deep work in you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I watching God from a safe distance rather than entering fully in?
What would it look like to give God sustained, unhurried time this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I do not want to observe You from a distance. Give me courage to enter in and stay, abiding in You long enough for Your work to go deep in me. Amen.
